children: Shares in Akamai Technologies jumped premarket after the cloud-computing company signed a deal worth at least $11.6 billion with frontier artificial-intelligence company Anthropic.
The stock surged 21% to $133.50 in premarket trade following the announcement of the deal after the closing bell Thursday.

Cambridge, Mass.-based Akamai will lease its central processing units and software to Anthropic over seven years, with the deal providing for a potential $9 billion expansion. The deal also gives Anthropic the right to buy up to 5% of Akamai's shares at $111.33 each. The price is a 0.8% premium to Akamai's closing share price of $110.41 on Thursday.

The deal will drive profits in Akamai's cloud-infrastructure division materially higher, J.P. Morgan analysts wrote in a note to clients. However, the tie-up leaves Akamai dependent on Anthropic, with the AI company now comprising 93% of Akamai's $14.4 billion in committed capacity contracts signed this year, the analysts said.

Because of the timing of Anthropic's payment, the deal means that Akamai will likely have to raise additional capital over the next year--a reality that could place temporary pressure on the company's margins, the analysts added.
The deal would add around $1.7 billion to Akamai's capital expenditures this year but won't change its full-year revenue guidance, the company said.
